newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish ERM entry may not be ripe just yet - ETLA.
newsitem.headline: Finnish ERM entry may not be ripe just yet - ETLA.

text.p: The time for the markka to join Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) might be ripe only after October 20 municipal and European Parliament elections, a leading Finnish economic think-tank said on Thursday.
"The time for entering the ERM might not be ripe until after the EU and municipal elections on October 20," the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) said in a financial markets review.
If export companies continued to convert currency earnings into markka, the Finnish unit would go on strengthening, ETLA said.
"If the markka is pegged (before the elections) at its current level, the markka might begin to appreciate owing to the snowballing effect of export firms repatriating their earnings," it said.
"The election debate would then focus, from the government's viewpoint, too much upon the negative impact of the ERM entry at this pivotal point in the business cycle," ETLA added.
Of key importance for the timing of ERM entry would be "how long the export companies will be patient to stand by and wait before repatriating their export earnings," it said.
ETLA warned against hoping for a depreciation of the markka.

"If the government and central bank hope that the markka will weaken before entering the ERM, the strategy may backfire," it said, adding: "Despite the lowering of interest rates, the markka remains under pressure to appreciate."
The Finnish unit was still over 20 percent weaker against the mark than before the November 1991 devaluation, ETLA noted.
